title: Help messages
description: Maps every consumer-facing message id of the copy catalog (conformance/parity/copy.en.json) and of the customer portal's own error copy to the Help page that explains it. The id is the heading anchor and the /docs/help/code/<id>/ redirect path: an id's anchor is /docs/help/messages/<page>/#<id>, where the page of a developerOnly id is `other`. DOC-03a owns the shape; DOC-05a fills the data.

pages.description: The pages under help/messages/, by file name without extension. `index` is the A to Z index.

group.description: The Help task group the page sits last in (docs plan section 3.2).

portal.description: The customer portal's own error copy (packages/admin/src/portal/errors.ts), keyed as that file keys it: a code, `status-<n>` for an HTTP status, `default`. Each key is the message id `portal.<key>`. helpMessages.test.ts fails when this mirror and errors.ts disagree.

messages.description: One entry per message id, in the order the pages show them. A catalog `codes` key is its own id (server codes use `_`, client codes use `-`); a `gate` or `activation` key is prefixed with its group and a dot; the fallback is `fallback`; a portal error is `portal.<key>`.

entry.description: Ids that carry the same on-screen title share one heading: give them the same `entry`, named after the first of them, which owns the heading and its anchor. Every id keeps its own anchor.

article.description: A shipped Help article (path under help/) this message links to.

why.description: Why you see this: one or two plain sentences. Held by the first id of each distinct on-screen message; the other ids that show the same message share it.

fix.description: What to do: one or two plain sentences. Held like `why`.

developerOnly.description: Ids listed under Other messages as developer-only: the app's developer needs to fix them. They have no entry of their own.
